coverage_notes: Both files read in full (500 top-level threads each, with all replies; 8VZIAknB-Ag.txt lines 1-2483, p8sRNKTGj9g.txt lines 1-1980). Counts are approximate hand-coding from reading, not keyword counts. Video 1 (narcissistic siblings) is overwhelmingly about childhood family abuse, estrangement and no-contact, not caregiving; only a small minority describe eldercare or estate matters. Video 2 (aging parents, posted by a menopause physician) is almost entirely caregivers of aging parents, so it carries nearly all the caregiving evidence; many commenters are women in their 40s-60s who also mention menopause. gap_evidence lists: paying_for_tools has only paying for human services and insurance, nothing about paying for software or apps. logins_passwords has only patient portals and an adult child doing a parent's online tasks; no shared-password talk. Replies are located as COMMENT n (reply).

videos.title: Keeping the PEACE with narcissistic siblings
videos.how_counted: Approximate. Own-situation here means a commenter describing caring for an aging or dying parent or relative, or handling an estate or parent's finances, with a sibling. Roughly 300 of 500 threads are childhood abuse, no-contact or validation and are coded T14 (family conflict not about caregiving), not counted as caregiving.
videos.audience_note: Viewers of a psychologist's video on narcissistic siblings: adult survivors of dysfunctional families. Caregiving shows up only at the edges: who did the work when a parent was dying, who controls parent money, estate fights after a parent's death, siblings who vanish then reappear. Treat as family-conflict evidence, not general caregiver evidence.

videos.title: Dealing with aging parents:  Is anyone else going through this?
videos.how_counted: Approximate hand-coding; one comment can carry several themes. Many comments are short solidarity statements (me too, 47 and dealing with this) that still count as own situation. T14 is mostly menopause/HRT overlapping with caregiving, plus fear of becoming a burden and planning own old age.
videos.audience_note: Audience of a menopause physician; mostly women in their 40s-60s who are daughters, daughters-in-law or wives caring for parents with dementia, frailty, cancer or stroke. Skews to dementia and to caregivers who are also working and raising kids (sandwich generation). Many are past caregivers writing after the parent died. Skews to people who are engaged with online health content.

new_themes.name: Caregiving collides with the caregiver's own midlife health
new_themes.description: Commenters describe doing parent care at the same time as their own menopause, illness, surgery or collapse of health, and say they cannot attend to their own appointments.

example.quote: It began with my in-laws at the very same time I began having HORRIFIC peri/menopause symptoms.

new_themes.name: Fear of becoming a burden / preparing own old age
new_themes.description: Caregivers say the experience changes how they plan their own aging, to spare their children.

example.quote: Listenng to you I just hope I wont be a burden to my kids. This is my primary reason why I really care about my health

new_themes.name: Losing the person twice (anticipatory grief)
new_themes.description: Grief for the parent as the person they knew before death, especially with dementia.

example.quote: It (Alzheimer’s) was so painful and heartbreaking because it’s like losing someone twice.

new_themes.name: Parents had no plan
new_themes.description: Parents did not plan finances, housing, legal papers or wishes, so the adult child improvises under pressure.

example.quote: The biggest problem is that all three did not have a plan in place to take care of themselves!!

new_themes.name: Lack of information and support
new_themes.description: Commenters say there is little information, no manual and little help for caregivers.

example.quote: Yes!!! and there are so little Support and Information out there to help.

new_themes.name: Caring for several people at once
new_themes.description: Caregivers handle two or more parents, in-laws, an aunt or a spouse at the same time, across households.

example.quote: You aren't alone! We have four going at the same time plus an elderly bachelor uncle.

new_themes.name: Estate and inheritance conflict after caregiving
new_themes.description: The sibling who did the care is blamed, cut out of the funeral or the will, or fights over property and the estate after the parent dies (mostly in the narcissistic-siblings video).

example.quote: I need to work with my narcissistic brother now that we’re in the estate process. It’s horrible.

new_themes.name: Caregiving not recognized by others
new_themes.description: Caregivers say others minimize their load or the system gives them no support.

example.quote: I’ve had to deal with people minimizing what I have had to do just because I have not had kids.

caveats: Public YouTube comments; self-selected, not a sample. Video 1 is mostly not about caregiving. Video 2 skews to women 40-65, daughters, dementia and people engaged with a women's health channel; many are past caregivers writing after a parent died. Counts are my approximate reading counts. Commenters are anonymous and unverified. Nothing in either file speaks to paying for software, shared passwords, or specific caregiving apps; the only named supports are the GUIDE Program, A Place for Mom, a medication dispenser, home cameras and patient portals. Dates in the files run to Oct 2026.
